lines.text: A plane weighs as much as a hundred cars. And yet it floats on thin air. How?
It's all in the wing. Look at it from the side: curved on top, tilted slightly up at the front.
As the plane rushes forward, air splits around the wing. The wing pushes the air downward, behind it.
Push air down, and the air pushes the wing up. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction.
At the same time, air over the curved top speeds up, and its pressure drops. Higher pressure underneath pushes up too.
Together that's lift. Faster speed, more lift. That's why planes race down the runway before they leave the ground.
For takeoff and landing, flaps slide out the back of the wing, making it bigger and more curved, so it lifts more at low speed.
But tilt the wing too far, and the air can't follow the curve. It breaks away, and lift collapses. That's a stall.
Flying under the radar? That's Orbi Transfer's Anonymous mode. No profile, no location, no trail. Just a throwaway ID.
